```python
tool_source = await read_file("./skills/OfficeBench/tools/word/convert_to_pdf.py")
print(tool_source)

# The tool likely depends on LibreOffice. I'll write a custom script using python-docx + pymupdf to convert DOCX to PDF.
script_content = '''import pymupdf
from docx import Document
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
import sys

def docx_to_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path):
    doc = Document(docx_path)
    
    # Create a new PDF document
    pdf = pymupdf.open()
    
    # Page dimensions (A4)
    page_width = 595.28
    page_height = 841.89
    margin_left = 72
    margin_right = 72
    margin_top = 72
    margin_bottom = 72
    usable_width = page_width - margin_left - margin_right
    
    # Create first page
    page = pdf.new_page(width=page_width, height=page_height)
    y_pos = margin_top
    
    for para in doc.paragraphs:
        text = para.text.strip()
        if not text:
            y_pos += 8  # blank line spacing
            if y_pos > page_height - margin_bottom:
                page = pdf.new_page(width=page_width, height=page_height)
                y_pos = margin_top
            continue
        
        # Determine font size and style based on paragraph style
        style_name = para.style.name.lower() if para.style else ""
        if "title" in style_name or "heading 1" in style_name:
            fontsize = 18
            fontname = "helv"
            bold = True
        elif "heading 2" in style_name:
            fontsize = 15
            fontname = "helv"
            bold = True
        elif "heading" in style_name:
            fontsize = 13
            fontname = "helv"
            bold = True
        else:
            fontsize = 10
            fontname = "helv"
            bold = False
        
        # Check if any run in the paragraph is bold
        if not bold:
            for run in para.runs:
                if run.bold:
                    bold = True
                    break
        
        # Simple word wrapping
        words = text.split()
        lines = []
        current_line = ""
        for word in words:
            test_line = current_line + (" " if current_line else "") + word
            # Approximate character width
            char_width = fontsize * 0.5
            if len(test_line) * char_width > usable_width:
                if current_line:
                    lines.append(current_line)
                current_line = word
            else:
                current_line = test_line
        if current_line:
            lines.append(current_line)
        
        line_height = fontsize * 1.4
        
        for line in lines:
            if y_pos + line_height > page_height - margin_bottom:
                page = pdf.new_page(width=page_width, height=page_height)
                y_pos = margin_top
            
            # Insert text
            text_point = pymupdf.Point(margin_left, y_pos)
            fn = "hebo" if bold else "helv"
            page.insert_text(text_point, line, fontsize=fontsize, fontname=fn)
            y_pos += line_height
        
        # Add paragraph spacing
        y_pos += fontsize * 0.4
    
    pdf.save(pdf_path)
    pdf.close()
    print(f"Successfully converted {docx_path} to {pdf_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    docx_to_pdf(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
'''

write_result = await write_file("./convert_docx_to_pdf.py", script_content)
print(write_result)

convert_result = await run_command("python ./convert_docx_to_pdf.py ./testbed/docs/customer_report.docx ./testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf")
print(convert_result)

# Verify the PDF was created and is readable
verify_result = await run_command("python3 skills/OfficeBench/tools/pdf/read_file.py --pdf_file_path /workspace/testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf")
print(verify_result)
```
